verdict.rationale_short: The Iran 60-day ceasefire framework (deal signing anticipated this weekend via VP Vance/Witkoff in Europe) sent Brent down to $86.91 (−2.9% from the June 11 close of $89.52), clearing the $97 oil regime trigger by a 10-point margin — the single most important regime development since Iran escalation began in late February. Asia responded with the strongest session in weeks: Nikkei +2.87%, Hang Seng +2.03%. ES futures are +0.41% to ~7,425, within 35 points of the 7,460 regime floor. SPCX — the $75B / $1.75T SpaceX IPO — begins its Nasdaq debut today with only a 4% float; extreme intraday volatility and multiple halts are expected. Three regime indicators remain in breach or at threshold: VIX 19.44 (above 18 trigger, ticking higher despite the rally — pre-FOMC caution), 30Y ~5.02% (above 5.0% threshold on sticky pipeline inflation), and DXY 100.04 (marginally above 100); SPX pre-market sits 35 points below the 7,460 floor. No major macro data today — CPI was June 10, PPI was June 11. Next fulcrum: FOMC June 16–17 (Warsh's first meeting; 98.3% probability of a hold, but hawkish bias shift possible after PPI +6.5% YoY + CPI 4.2% YoY). HOLD at medium conviction: do not chase the open, do not buy SPCX on day one. The BUY upgrade requires formal Iran deal signing this weekend + SPX closing above 7,460 + VIX below 17 + a neutral FOMC from Warsh.

dont_buy.reason: The largest IPO in history begins trading today with only ~4% of shares in public float — roughly $3B of the $75B raise in public hands, against $250B+ in oversubscribed demand. With MSCI passive inclusion flow not starting until June 13 and institutional allocatees subject to lock-ups, the open-market supply/demand dynamic on day 1 is entirely unpredictable. The opening print could spike to $155–175 before collapsing to $130 in the same session — no directional edge without allocation knowledge.
dont_buy.better_entry: Day 3–5 after initial float normalization; the structural MSCI passive inclusion bid is durable but requires patience; analyst week-1 price target range is $140–175 — that range encompasses most of the risk/reward without day-1 volatility

bear_case: The 60-day Iran ceasefire announced June 11 is structurally identical to three prior ceasefire frameworks (April 7, April 21, May 29) that each collapsed within 48–96 hours — in each case, oil snapped back to prior highs within a week and Brent returned above $93. The naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz remains in force by Trump's explicit statement until the deal is 'finalized,' which has not occurred; Iranian officials stated as recently as June 11 that 'no final decision has been reached.' If the Vance signing collapses over the weekend, Brent snaps from $86.91 back toward $92–95, re-approaching the $97 oil trigger with 24 hours' notice. The VIX at 19.44 is a technical warning sign: volatility is firming into the FOMC despite the rally, not compressing — the market is pricing deal risk, not deal certainty. FOMC June 16–17 introduces an independent tail: Warsh's first meeting with a stagflationary data set (PPI +6.5% YoY, CPI 4.2% YoY) provides empirical cover for a hawkish bias shift from neutral-to-easing to neutral-to-tightening; if the dot plot signals a hike in September, the 30Y spikes above 5.15% and SPX retreats 200+ points below the 7,460 floor before Thursday's close. **Invalidation: If Iran deal is formally signed with Hormuz reopening commitment this weekend AND Warsh delivers a neutral-to-dovish FOMC statement on June 17 AND 30Y falls below 4.80%, HOLD converts to BUY at Monday June 16 open. If Iran deal collapses AND Brent re-approaches $93+, HOLD converts to STEP ASIDE immediately.**
